feature.summary: Controls who may chat with an agent: only the owner, named workspace members, or everyone in the workspace. Sharing needs a workspace and a published version. Web and Mobile support it against our servers. A public directory does not exist. CLI agents are private by file location.

purpose.what_it_does: The owner sets visibility to private, people or workspace. For people, named workspace members get an access row. Those people (or all members) can chat with the published version, read-only. (apps/web/lib/services/custom-agent-service.ts:561-600; apps/web/db/neon/0370_user_agents.sql:18-22).
purpose.why_it_exists: Teams want to reuse one assistant. Private-only agents force copying instructions around (migration purpose, 0370_user_agents.sql:1-9; brief S52.31 to S52.34).
purpose.who_uses_it: Owners who build agents for a workspace; teammates who use them.
problems_solved: Choosing a few people rather than the whole workspace.
use_cases: Share a drafting agent with three teammates.
Share an onboarding agent with the whole workspace.
Keep a personal prompt helper private.
In the CLI, commit a project agent file so the team inherits it.

where_to_find_it: Web: open an agent, Agent tab, section 'Sharing' with radio choices and 'Save sharing' (apps/web/features/agents/components/AgentPublishPanel.tsx:192-299).
Web list: sections 'Your agents' and 'Shared with you' (apps/web/features/agents/components/AgentsPage.tsx:219-230).

Mobile: Sharing section with chips 'Only you', 'Specific people', and the workspace name; list sections 'Your agents', 'Shared with you', 'Retired' (apps/mobile/src/features/agents/components/AgentManageSections.tsx:55-59, 302-400; AgentsScreen.tsx:80-102).
CLI: no sharing command; scope is the folder: project .agiworkforce/agents or global (apps/cli/src/agents.rs:258-268, 1062-1090).
Desktop Tauri: scope radio global or project when creating (apps/desktop/src/features/settings/CustomAgentEditor.tsx:272-285).
prerequisites: Agent lives in a workspace (organization); personal-space agents stay private (service:569-573).
screens_and_controls: Radio options: 'Only you' (help 'Nobody else can see or use it.'), 'Specific people' (help 'Members of this workspace you pick can chat with the published version.'), 'Everyone in the workspace' plus ' in <workspace name>' (AgentPublishPanel.tsx:19-31, 234-236).
Checkbox list of workspace members with name and email when 'Specific people' is chosen (AgentPublishPanel.tsx:249-284).
'Save sharing' button, enabled only when something changed and the agent is published (AgentPublishPanel.tsx:285-296).

Notices: 'Personal agents stay private. Create it in a workspace to share it.', 'Publish the agent before you share it.', 'Nobody else is in this workspace yet.' (AgentPublishPanel.tsx:211-213, 244-248, 250-253).
Recipient view: label 'Shared by <name>', read-only form, line '<name> built this agent. Only its owner can change it.' (agent-display.ts:22; AgentEditorPage.tsx:416-420).
journey: Create the agent inside a workspace and publish it (see F052-09).
Open the Sharing section and choose who can use it.
Teammates see it under 'Shared with you' and press Chat; chats run the published version.
To stop sharing, choose 'Only you' and save, or retire the agent.
feedback_and_outputs: Toasts 'Sharing saved.' and 'Sharing could not be saved.' (AgentPublishPanel.tsx:134, 136).

Server messages: 'Agents in your personal space stay private. Create it in a workspace to share it.', 'Publish the agent before you share it.', 'Choose at least one person to share with.' (service:570-583).
A workspace audit event 'agent_shared' is recorded with the visibility and head count (apps/web/app/api/custom-agents/[id]/share/route.ts:89-98).
Recipient list label 'Shared by <name>' or 'Shared with you'.
settings: Visibility value private, people or workspace (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/agents.ts:12).
Up to 100 named people per share (agents.ts:28).

working: Share route GET returns visibility, workspace name and the first 100 other members with a hasAccess flag; PUT validates and saves (apps/web/app/api/custom-agents/[id]/share/route.ts:71-100).

shareAgent runs in a transaction: needs a workspace, a published version and at least one person for 'people'; updates visibility; deletes access rows not in the list; inserts new ones (service:561-600).

Database rules: non-private needs organization_id (0370_user_agents.sql:72-73); recipients can read only published, non-retired agents in the current workspace, and for 'people' only with an access row (policy lines 185-206); only the owner can grant, and only to workspace members (lines 241-255).
The list shows the owner's agents plus others' agents in the current workspace (service:281-297).
Teammates run the published copy only (service:146-149).

Mobile has the same sharing control and also 'Report' and 'Hide' for a shared agent from a sharer (apps/mobile/src/features/agents/components/AgentManageSections.tsx:302-400; AgentEditorScreen.tsx:150-160).

CLI: an agent is private by where it is stored; project agents load only when the workspace is trusted and a project agent never replaces your own agent of the same name (agents.rs:258-274, tests at 2199, 2217).
incomplete: Share member list is limited to the first 100 workspace members with no paging (share route:46-51) [inferred: larger workspaces cannot pick everyone].
Switching visibility to 'workspace' does not remove old access rows? It does: access rows not in the new list are deleted, and the list is empty for non-people (service:577, 585-589).

Brief cites agents.rs:228 and :255 for workspace access; those lines are in subagent application and discovery code, not sharing. The nearest CLI idea is project scope shared by committing the file [inferred].
disconnected_or_disabled: Brief marks Web and Mobile 'missing' while code works.
not_available: Public listing or directory of agents: no code found (S52.34). The mobile 'By <company>' group is a fixed built-in list in code, not user listings (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/agent-catalog.ts:5-17).
Sharing from CLI, desktop file editor, VS Code or Chrome.
Sharing with people outside the workspace, or by link: not found.

established.statement: An assistant can be kept private to its creator.
A builder can share an assistant with named people.
A builder can make an assistant available to everyone in their workspace.
A builder can list an assistant in a public directory others can browse.
Workspace and role rules decide who may read a resource; sharing a Local item to another boundary needs consent.
Custom GPTs and the GPT Store are a migration source, not the enduring target architecture, so a public store is not assumed.

acceptance_criteria: A new agent is private: another workspace member does not see it in 'Shared with you'.
Sharing before publishing is refused with 'Publish the agent before you share it.'
A personal-space agent cannot be shared and the panel says so.
'Specific people' with nobody ticked is refused.
After sharing with person A only, person B cannot read or chat with the agent (route and database both refuse).
After 'Everyone in the workspace', every member sees it; after 'Only you', they no longer do.
A recipient cannot edit, publish, share, transfer or delete.
Retiring the agent removes it from recipients.
inferred: Sharing should extend to every app that can run an agent; VS Code and Chrome do not list agents today [inferred].
The 100-person cap and member listing should page for larger workspaces [inferred].
A public directory, if wanted, needs review, reporting and a separate visibility value; none exists [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Add paging and search to the people picker.
[proposed] Decide on public listing in a decision record before building, given the product direction on GPT stores.
[proposed] Show the owner who currently has access in the list row.

steps.what_happens: Owner opens the Sharing section; the client fetches GET share to get visibility, workspace name and members.
Owner saves; PUT sends visibility and user ids; the server checks ownership, workspace, published version and people count, then updates user_agents and user_agent_access in one transaction.
A recipient's list call returns agents in the current workspace; database policies filter what they may read; presentation hides unpublished data.
The recipient starts a chat: a conversation row is made with the agent id and each turn loads the published copy.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Sharing does not involve a model. Recipients' chats use the owner's pinned model only when their chat is on Auto (agent-turn-config.ts:175-182); billing for the recipient's turns is not described in the agent code: unknown.

access_and_usage.account: Signed in on Web or Mobile; the recipient must be a member of the workspace.
access_and_usage.permissions: Only the owner changes sharing (requireOwnedAgent). Grant only to workspace members (policy lines 241-255). Recipients are read-only (AgentEditorPage.tsx:184).
access_and_usage.subscription: No plan gate found on sharing. Workspace membership comes from team plans [inferred]; Team and Enterprise tiers carry team admin (billing-catalog.ts:358).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Up to 100 people per share (agents.ts:28). Optional per-person daily message cap and workspace-wide monthly credit cap set by the owner apply to recipients (agent-turn-config.ts:81-100).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Sharing exists only for Cloud agents. Mobile Local mode shows the gate 'Agents run in AGI Cloud' (AgentEditorScreen.tsx:79-90). CLI project agents are shared by the repository, outside the product.

corrections.claim: The list shows the owner's agents plus others' agents in the current workspace (service:281-297)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The query selects other users' agents in the workspace with no visibility, published or access filter, and caps at 500 rows. Row-level security does the filtering, so the SQL does not filter by visibility.
corrections.correction: The list query returns the owner's agents in the current organization (or personal space) plus any other user's agents with organization_id equal to the current workspace, limit 500. The database row policy decides which of those the viewer may read.

corrections.claim: Share route GET returns visibility, workspace name and the first 100 other members with a hasAccess flag
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The service lists up to 100 members (AGENT_SHARE_PEOPLE_MAX) and then filters out the owner, so at most 100 and usually 99 others. GET also returns an empty member list and null workspace name when the owner is no longer an active member.
corrections.correction: GET returns visibility, workspace name and members from the first page of 100 workspace members with the owner removed. It returns no members or workspace name if the owner's membership is not active.

corrections.claim: Local mode: Sharing exists only for Cloud agents. Mobile Local mode shows the gate 'Agents run in AGI Cloud' (AgentEditorScreen.tsx:79-90)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The gate (CloudFeatureGate with 'Agents run in AGI Cloud; switching won't upload your local chats.') is at AgentEditorScreen.tsx:66-75, not 79-90. It is shown when !access.ready, not only in Local mode. The list screen has the same gate at AgentsScreen.tsx:495.
corrections.correction: Mobile shows a CloudFeatureGate ('Agents run in AGI Cloud; switching won't upload your local chats.') whenever cloud access is not ready (Local mode or signed out), on both the editor and the list screen. Cite AgentEditorScreen.tsx:66-75.

corrections.claim: Optional per-person daily message cap and workspace-wide monthly credit cap set by the owner apply to recipients (agent-turn-config.ts:81-100)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The daily cap is counted per user and agent (countAgentTurnsToday(db,userId,agentId)). The monthly cap is spend against the single agent id (readAgentMonthSpendMicrousd(db, agentId)). It is per agent across all users, not workspace-wide. Both are skipped when null.
corrections.correction: The daily cap is per person per agent and resets at midnight UTC. The monthly credit cap is per agent, summed over everyone who uses it, and resets on the 1st UTC. It is not a workspace-wide cap.

corrections.claim: Subscription: Team and Enterprise tiers carry team admin (billing-catalog.ts:358)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The billing-catalog.ts at the cited line sits in packages/contracts/types/src/, not apps/web/lib. Line 358 is `managed_api: PRO_TIERS`, not a team-admin entry. The cite does not support the claim.
corrections.correction: Cite the real file path and the line that defines team features, or drop the sentence. No plan gate on sharing was found; membership comes from the organization_members table.

missing_facts: The access-row delete runs when ownership is transferred, but it is not the only revoke path. Switching to 'workspace' or 'private' deletes all access rows because the people list is empty (custom-agent-service.ts:577-589). The page covers this, but it also states a false doubt about it in the 'Incomplete' list.

The monthly credit limit is spent per agent across all users, so one heavy recipient can lock out every other recipient for the month (agent-turn-config.ts:91-100). The page calls it workspace-wide, which hides this.

GET share returns an empty member list and null workspace name when the owner is no longer an active workspace member, so an owner who has left the workspace cannot pick people (apps/web/app/api/custom-agents/[id]/share/route.ts:40-44). The page does not mention it.
